title: Polynomial-length choice scheduling
statement: For all natural numbers $C$ and $c$, there exist a finite deterministic Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a natural number $A$ such that, for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, if $x$ is the all-$1$ word of length $n$ and $T=A(n+1)^{c+1}$, then both of the following hold: every choice word of length $T$ drives the guessing-phase machine of $M$ from its initial configuration on $x$ to the configuration corresponding to the $T$-step run of $M$, with some captured word of length exactly $C(n+1)^c$; and every word of length exactly $C(n+1)^c$ is captured in such a configuration by some choice word of length $T$.
hypotheses_covered: $x$ is the all-$1$ Boolean word of length $n$
replaced: For all natural numbers $C$ and $c$ there exist a deterministic scheduler machine $M$ and a constant $A$ such that for every $n$, on the unary input of length $n$ and with $T = A(n+1)^{c+1}$: every choice word of length $T$ drives the guessing-phase machine of $M$ to the completed $T$-step configuration while capturing some word of length exactly $C(n+1)^c$, and every word of that length is captured by some choice word of length $T$.
